able.en: having the power to do something

noteEs.usage: Casi siempre en bear/take the brunt of.

noteHi.meaning: किसी नुकसान या बोझ का सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा।
noteHi.usage: लगभग हमेशा bear/take the brunt of में आता है।

noteJa.meaning: 打撃や負担の最も大きな部分。
noteJa.usage: ほぼ bear/take the brunt of の形で使う。

noteKo.usage: 거의 bear/take the brunt of 형태로 쓴다.

brunt.zh: 最大衝擊（bear the brunt：首當其衝）

noteHi.exampleTr: तनाव आपके स्वास्थ्य के लिए हानिकारक हो सकता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: ストレスは健康に有害になりうる。

diagnosis.en: finding out what illness someone has

note.meaning: 停止；中止（使用、生產或服務）。
note.usage: 正式用語，及物動詞，常見 discontinue a product/service/use。

noteEn.meaning: to stop using, making or offering something.

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa dejará de fabricar el modelo antiguo el próximo año.
noteEs.meaning: suspender; dejar de usar o producir.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी अगले साल पुराना मॉडल बंद कर देगी।

noteJa.exampleTr: その会社は来年旧モデルの製造を中止する。

noteEs.exampleTr: El trabajo implica trabajar los fines de semana.
noteEs.usage: entail sth/doing; como involve pero formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: इस नौकरी में सप्ताहांत पर काम करना शामिल है।
noteHi.meaning: आवश्यक रूप से शामिल करता है।
noteHi.usage: entail sth/doing; involve जैसा औपचारिक शब्द।

noteJa.exampleTr: その仕事には週末勤務が伴う。

examining.ex: Police are examining the CCTV footage.

face.zh: 面臨；（in the face of：面對）

noteEs.usage: Se usa finite resources; lo contrario: infinite.

noteHi.exampleTr: सूखे इलाक़ों में पानी सीमित संसाधन है।
noteHi.usage: finite resources आम है; उल्टा infinite।

noteJa.exampleTr: 乾燥地域では水は有限の資源だ。
noteJa.usage: finite resources の形が多い；反対は infinite。

noteKo.usage: finite resources 형태가 흔하다; 반대는 infinite.

noteHi.usage: औपचारिक शब्द; व्यवस्था, नीति या संसाधनों के बँटवारे के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 現在の資金モデルは非常に不公平だ。
noteJa.usage: 制度・政策・資源配分に使う硬い語。

number.ex: The number of visitors fell this year.

obliged.ex: You are not obliged to answer.

officials.en: people who work for a government

private.en: owned by one person, not shared

produce.ex: The council will produce a new guide.

prompted.ex: The storm prompted the school to close early.

put.ex: Parents put pressure on the school.

quantified.ex: The damage has not yet been quantified.

paragraphs: The HSE runs the health service in Ireland. It will stop a scheme for some older patients. Now, family doctors can send people over 60 for an MRI scan. This is for problems with the hip or knee. Soon, this will end.
About 21,000 of these scans happen every year. The HSE says many older people do not need them. A doctor can often find the problem with a normal check or an X-ray.
Patients can still get an MRI through a hospital specialist. But hospital waiting lists can be very long.
Some doctors are not happy. They say family doctors will have to give patients the bad news. A Labour politician, Marie Sherlock, says the change is unfair to older people without health insurance.
sentZh: HSE負責管理愛爾蘭的醫療服務。
它將停止一項針對部分年長病患的計畫。

HSE表示，許多年長者並不需要做這種掃描。
醫師通常用一般檢查或X光就能找出問題。
病患仍然可以透過醫院的專科醫師做MRI。
但醫院的候診名單可能非常長。
有些醫師並不滿意。
他們說，家庭醫師將不得不向病患傳達這個壞消息。
工黨政治人物瑪麗・夏洛克表示，這項改變對沒有健康保險的年長者不公平。

paragraphs: The HSE is going to end a scheme that lets family doctors, or GPs, send patients over 60 for MRI scans in the community. The scheme is for people with hip and knee problems. About 21,000 of these scans are done each year.

The HSE says it made the decision after checking the scheme earlier this year. It says the change is based on medical evidence. For most older people with worn hip or knee joints, an MRI scan is not usually needed. Doctors can normally find the problem by examining the patient or by using a simple X-ray.

The HSE also says the number of MRI scanners is limited, so it wants to use them better. An internal report from 30 October said the HSE is working out how much money the change will save. Overall, the community scheme provides 240,000 scans a year.
Patients will still be able to get an MRI if a hospital specialist asks for one. But that usually means joining a hospital waiting list.

Prof Tadhg Crowley, who leads the GP committee of the Irish Medical Organisation, says the change will put pressure on family doctors. They will have to tell patients that the service has ended. He wants the HSE to make information for patients instead.

Labour's health spokeswoman, Marie Sherlock, called the cut unfair to older people. She said people without health insurance could wait 18 months or more. She also said spending on private scans was 21 per cent over budget at the end of September.

這項計畫是給有髖部和膝蓋問題的人。
這類掃描每年大約做21,000次。
HSE表示，它是在今年稍早檢查這項計畫後做出這個決定的。
它說這項改變是根據醫學證據。

他希望改由HSE為病患製作說明資料。
工黨衛生發言人瑪麗・夏洛克稱這項刪減對年長者不公平。
她說沒有健康保險的人可能要等18個月或更久。
她還說，到9月底，私人掃描的支出已超出預算21%。

paragraphs: The HSE is to end a scheme that allows GPs to refer patients over the age of 60 with hip and knee problems for MRI scans in the community. Around 21,000 such scans are carried out every year.

The health service said the decision followed an audit earlier this year and was based largely on clinical evidence. According to the HSE, MRI scans are not routinely needed for older adults with osteoarthritis in the hip or knee. In most cases, a diagnosis can be made through a clinical examination and, if necessary, a standard X-ray.

The HSE added that MRI capacity is limited and that the change would make better use of radiology resources. An internal financial report dated 30 October said officials were still estimating the savings. The wider community diagnostics scheme delivers about 240,000 scans a year.
Patients will still be able to receive MRI scans if they are referred through specialist hospital services. However, critics point out that this often means long waiting lists.

Prof Tadhg Crowley, chairman of the Irish Medical Organisation's GP committee, warned that family doctors would be left to explain the change to patients. He called on the HSE to produce clear information material instead.

Labour health spokeswoman Marie Sherlock described the cut as regressive and unfair to older people. She said those without health insurance could face waits of 18 months or longer, and claimed that spending on private imaging was 21 per cent over budget by the end of September.

每年約進行21,000次這類掃描。
衛生服務機構表示，這項決定是在今年稍早的一次審查之後做出的，主要依據臨床證據。
根據HSE的說法，髖部或膝部有骨關節炎的年長者通常不需要例行做MRI掃描。
在大多數情況下，透過臨床檢查，必要時再加上標準X光，就能做出診斷。
HSE補充說，MRI的容量有限，這項改變能更好地利用放射科資源。
一份日期為10月30日的內部財務報告說，官員仍在估算可節省的金額。
範圍更廣的社區診斷計畫每年提供約24萬次掃描。
如果病患透過醫院專科服務轉介，仍可接受MRI掃描。
然而，批評者指出，這往往意味著漫長的候診名單。
愛爾蘭醫學組織家庭醫師委員會主席泰格・克勞利教授警告，向病患解釋這項改變的工作將落在家庭醫師身上。
他呼籲HSE改為製作清楚的說明資料。
工黨衛生發言人瑪麗・夏洛克形容這項刪減是開倒車，且對年長者不公平。
她說沒有健康保險的人可能要等待18個月或更久，並聲稱到9月底，私人影像檢查的支出已超出預算21%。

paragraphs: The HSE is set to scrap a scheme under which GPs could refer patients over 60 with hip and knee complaints directly for community-based MRI scans. Roughly 21,000 such scans are performed annually.

The health service insists the move stems from an audit conducted earlier this year and rests largely on clinical evidence. In its view, MRI is seldom warranted for older adults with osteoarthritis of the hip or knee, since a diagnosis can typically be reached through a physical examination and, where required, a conventional X-ray.

Officials also stress that MRI capacity is finite and that scarce radiology resources must be deployed more judiciously. An internal financial report dated 30 October indicated that the HSE was still quantifying the likely savings. The broader community diagnostics programme delivers some 240,000 scans each year.
Patients will still have access to MRI if they are referred through specialist pathways, although critics note that this frequently entails joining lengthy hospital queues.

Prof Tadhg Crowley, who chairs the Irish Medical Organisation's GP committee, cautioned that family doctors would bear the brunt of breaking the news to patients. He urged the HSE to take responsibility for communicating the change itself.

Labour health spokeswoman Marie Sherlock condemned the cut as regressive and inequitable. She argued that people without private health insurance could languish on waiting lists for 18 months or more, and alleged that outlays on private imaging had overshot their budget by 21 per cent by the end of September.

這類掃描每年大約進行21,000次。
衛生服務機構堅稱，此舉源自今年稍早進行的一次審查，主要以臨床證據為基礎。
在它看來，髖或膝骨關節炎的年長者很少有必要做MRI，因為通常透過身體檢查，必要時再加上傳統X光，就能做出診斷。

他敦促HSE自行負起說明這項改變的責任。
工黨衛生發言人瑪麗・夏洛克譴責這項刪減是開倒車且不公平。
她認為，沒有私人健康保險的人可能在候診名單上苦等18個月或更久，並指稱到9月底，私人影像檢查的支出已超出預算21%。

paragraphs: The HSE intends to discontinue a scheme that enabled GPs to refer patients aged over 60 with hip and knee conditions for MRI scans in community settings. Approximately 21,000 such scans are conducted each year.

According to the health service, the decision was prompted by an audit undertaken earlier this year and is predominantly grounded in clinical evidence. It maintains that MRI is not routinely indicated for older adults with osteoarthritis of the hip or knee; rather, a diagnosis can generally be established through clinical assessment and, where necessary, a plain X-ray.

The HSE further emphasises that MRI capacity is finite and that radiology resources must therefore be allocated more efficiently. An internal financial report dated 30 October noted that the anticipated savings had yet to be quantified. Overall, the community diagnostics scheme accounts for approximately 240,000 scans annually.
Access to MRI will remain available to patients referred through specialist pathways. Nevertheless, this route is frequently associated with substantial waiting times.

Prof Tadhg Crowley, chairman of the Irish Medical Organisation's GP committee, contended that the policy would place considerable pressure on general practitioners, who would be obliged to inform patients of the change. He maintained that the HSE should assume responsibility for producing appropriate patient communication materials.

Labour health spokeswoman Marie Sherlock characterised the cut as regressive and disproportionately detrimental to older people. She asserted that individuals without health insurance could face delays of 18 months or more, and noted that expenditure on third-party diagnostic imaging was 21 per cent over budget at the end of September.

這類掃描每年約進行21,000次。
根據衛生服務機構的說法，這項決定是由今年稍早進行的一次審查所促成，且主要以臨床證據為依據。

然而，這條途徑往往伴隨著相當長的等待時間。
愛爾蘭醫學組織家庭醫師委員會主席泰格・克勞利教授主張，這項政策會給全科醫師帶來相當大的壓力，因為他們將有義務告知病患這項改變。
他堅持HSE應負起製作適當病患說明資料的責任。
